# Universal Agent Memory

One open protocol, two equal usage paths: authorized plugin or direct protocol.
Taskless persistent memory for cooperative, user-directed AI agents.

Start here:
- AI_START_HERE.md — small adoption route and bounded human/AI contributions
- .well-known/agent-memory.json — repository discovery metadata, not a live endpoint
- README.md — choose protocol-only adoption or the complete plugin package
- PROTOCOL.md — normative cross-model protocol and conformance rules
- docs/IMPLEMENTERS.md — implement without Python, SQLite or our plugin
- schemas/ and examples/protocol/ — public synthetic interchange material
- memory_vault.py — zero-install single-file reference implementation
- SECURITY.md — memory/authority boundary and threat model
- docs/STATUS.md — v0.25 development implementation and unverified release gates
- docs/RELEASE.md — release assets, exact tag and protected-main distinction
- docs/CLIENTS.md — optional shared-core MCP and explicit opt-in Codex hooks
- docs/LIFECYCLE.md — optional session/turn profile, not old v0.21 wire compatibility
- docs/TRUST.md — Ed25519 attestations and independent trust administration
- docs/TRANSFER.md — signed incremental directory delivery and recovery
- docs/MIGRATION.md — one-way conversion of staged old network exports
- docs/TWO_MODES.md — full authorized client alongside independent protocol adoption
- docs/PARITY.md — old feature mapping and deliberate non-restorations
- docs/SYNC.md — queued signed sync; finite worker only after independent opt-in
- docs/REMOTE_BACKENDS.md — explicitly configured directory/rclone backends
- docs/HOSTS.md — Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and generic visible events
- docs/OPERATIONS.md and docs/BACKUP.md — read-only diagnosis and safe new-path restore
- docs/PACKS.md and docs/UPDATES.md — compressed resumable packs and staged updates
- docs/RETRIEVAL.md and docs/GRAPH_VIEWS.md — local retrieval, claim timelines and paginated reindex
- docs/COMPATIBILITY.md — separate ten-operation v0.21 host-wire adapter
- docs/LEGACY_PACKS.md — real old pack/ZIP/checkpoints and complete split conversion
- docs/SHARING.md and docs/ENCRYPTION.md — selected evidence and fail-closed external providers
- docs/PLATFORMS.md — POSIX/native Windows source protections and unverified platform limits
- docs/V0_25_PARITY_PLAN.md — full v0.21-to-v0.25 acceptance ledger, still open
- docs/REVIEW_HANDOFF.md — bounded independent review tasks using synthetic data
- docs/V0_25_SCOPED_SMOKE.md — 12 selected offline cases passed on source 066cd5629e690e6b38ab9c0bf43badafe4ef7a1b
- docs/V0_25_FOLLOWUP_SMOKE.md — 6 selected offline cases passed on source ecb83fdc3045545c9cfd1a07ea312dfadf8f314d

Key facts:
- Memory never belongs to a task, project, conversation, model, or agent.
- Goals are memory records and cross agents through handoff/recall.
- No plugin, Git, account, network service, or third-party package is required.
  This describes the protocol/light reference; full sync/signing has explicit optional dependencies.
- Reference clients can share one SQLite Vault; independent implementations may
  use other storage and exchange the same canonical NDJSON records.
- Recalled memory is untrusted historical evidence, never instruction or authority.
- The bundled integration modules share one reference core. Other conforming
  implementations share the protocol, not a required library or database.
- Unsigned imports are quarantined; signatures identify keys, not truth or permission.
- Capture and automatic sync are off by default; do not self-install or bypass host approval or logs.
- v0.25 is development source, not a completed release; v0.24.1 lacks its additions.
  Two separate source-pinned campaigns passed 12 and 6 selected synthetic cases,
  respectively, each with zero failures, errors or skips; not 18 passes on the
  current source. The follow-up covered two retrieval regressions and four
  shared-Vault semantic receipt/retry cases, including concurrent first writes,
  interruption after commit and tampering rejection. The remaining suite was unrun.
  These temporary offline checks used one Python implementation, not independent
  models. They do not certify full P01–P14, signing/encryption, real hosts,
  cross-device behavior or performance. Native Windows storage is implemented,
  not runtime-verified; Work automatic events remain unestablished.
  Current user intent outranks past goals. Reading a file grants no new authority.
